q: Consider the House of the People: 1-Its maximum strength at present is 552. 2-Not more than twenty members represent Union Territories. 3-Its present actual strength is 543. Which is/are correct?
expl: The maximum is 550 since nominated Anglo-Indian seats ended in 2020.
why: The figure 552 was accurate for seventy years and changed in 2020, which is why older material still prints it.
trapnote: Rebuild the ceiling from its components: 530 plus 20 equals 550. The old total is obsolete.

q: Consider the Council of States: 1-Its maximum strength is 250. 2-Twelve members are nominated by the President. 3-It may be dissolved by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Which is/are correct?
expl: It is a permanent body and is never dissolved.
why: The permanence of the upper House is structural, and one third of its members retire every second year.
trapnote: The upper House is never dissolved. Retirement by rotation is what keeps it continuous.

q: On the interval between sessions of Parliament, which statement is correct?
options: Parliament must hold at least three sessions in each calendar year
Six months may not elapse between the first sittings of two successive sessions
Parliament must sit for a minimum of one hundred days in each year
Six months may not elapse between the last sitting of one session and the first of the next
expl: The rule fixes the gap between the last sitting and the next first sitting.
why: Three sessions a year is convention and there is no minimum number of sitting days prescribed.
trapnote: The rule measures a gap, not a count. No minimum number of sittings is prescribed.

q: Consider a Money Bill: 1-It may be introduced only in the lower House. 2-The Speaker's certificate is declared final. 3-The upper House may amend it within fourteen days. Which is/are correct?
expl: The upper House may recommend but not amend, and must return the Bill within fourteen days.
why: The distinction between recommending and amending is the operative point and is easy to blur.
trapnote: The upper House recommends; it cannot amend or reject. Recommendations are not binding.

q: A Money Bill is not returned by the upper House within fourteen days. Which statement is correct?
options: It is deemed to have been passed by both Houses at the end of that period
It lapses and must be reintroduced in the lower House afresh
A joint sitting is summoned to resolve the resulting deadlock
It is referred to the President for a decision on the disagreement
expl: Non-return within fourteen days operates as deemed passage.
why: The third option applies the deadlock machinery, which is expressly unavailable for Money Bills.
trapnote: No deadlock can arise on a Money Bill, so the deadlock machinery has no application.

q: Consider a joint sitting: 1-It may be summoned for an ordinary Bill. 2-It may be summoned for a Money Bill. 3-It is presided over by the Speaker of the lower House. Which is/are correct?
expl: Ordinary Bills only, and the Speaker presides.
why: The upper House's presiding officer does not preside at a joint sitting, which is the structural surprise here.
trapnote: The Speaker presides at a joint sitting, not the Chairman of the upper House.

q: On parliamentary committees, which statement is correct?
options: The Public Accounts Committee has thirty members and the Estimates Committee twenty-two
Both committees have twenty-two members drawn from both Houses
Both committees have thirty members drawn from the lower House alone
The Public Accounts Committee has twenty-two members and the Estimates Committee thirty
expl: Twenty-two and thirty respectively, the Estimates Committee being drawn from the lower House alone.
why: The two numbers are the standard swap, and the single-House composition of one of them is a further point.
trapnote: Twenty-two for accounts and undertakings, thirty for estimates. Only estimates is single-House.

q: Consider the privilege of freedom from arrest enjoyed by a member: 1-It extends to civil cases. 2-It extends to criminal cases. 3-It extends to preventive detention. Which is/are correct?
expl: Only civil-case immunity holds; criminal and preventive custody are outside it.
why: This is the safeguard most often asserted in the field and most often misunderstood by officers.
trapnote: Civil process only. Criminal arrest is lawful, subject to informing the presiding officer.

q: A State Legislative Council is to be abolished. Which statement is correct?
options: The Assembly must pass a special-majority resolution and Parliament must then make a law
The Assembly's special-majority resolution by itself abolishes the Council
Parliament may abolish it by law without any resolution of the Assembly
Abolition requires ratification by not less than half the State legislatures
expl: The resolution is a precondition; Parliament's law is the operative act.
why: Andhra Pradesh illustrates the point: an abolition resolution of 2020 has not been acted on and the Council continues.
trapnote: The Assembly proposes and Parliament disposes. A resolution alone achieves nothing.

q: Consider the Andhra Pradesh legislature: 1-It is bicameral. 2-Its Assembly has 175 seats. 3-Its Council was abolished in 1985 and revived in 2007. Which is/are correct?
expl: All three are accurate.
why: The abolition and revival history is what makes the State the standard illustration of the abolition provision.
trapnote: Abolished 1985, revived 2007, and a further abolition resolution of 2020 remains unacted upon.

q: On the removal of the Speaker, which statement is correct?
options: Fourteen days' notice and a resolution passed by a special majority of the House
Seven days' notice and a resolution passed by an effective majority of the House
Fourteen days' notice and a resolution of both Houses sitting together
Fourteen days' notice and a resolution passed by an effective majority of the House
expl: Fourteen days' notice and an effective majority.
why: Effective majority means a majority of the members then in office, excluding vacancies.
trapnote: Effective majority is a distinct concept: a majority of the present strength of the House.

q: Consider the composition of a State Legislative Council: 1-It may not exceed one-third of the Assembly's strength. 2-It may not be fewer than forty members. 3-Its members are all directly elected. Which is/are correct?
expl: Its members are elected by various constituencies and some are nominated by the Governor.
why: The composition is mixed, which is precisely what distinguishes a Council from an Assembly.
trapnote: A Council is composed of several electorates plus nominees. It is not directly elected as a whole.

q: Consider the term of the House of the People: 1-Five years from the date of its first sitting. 2-Extendable by one year at a time during a Proclamation of Emergency. 3-Extendable by a resolution of the House itself. Which is/are correct?
expl: Extension requires a law of Parliament, not a resolution of the House.
why: The third statement is attractive because the House is the body affected, but it cannot extend its own life by resolution.
trapnote: Extension is by law and only during a Proclamation. The House cannot extend itself by resolution.

q: On the quorum for a sitting of either House, which statement is correct?
options: One-sixth of the total number of members of the House
One-fourth of the total number of members of the House
One-tenth of the total number of members of the House
Fifty members in the lower House and twenty-five in the upper House
expl: One-tenth of the total membership, including the presiding officer.
why: The fourth option gives absolute figures, which is how quorum is fixed in some other legislatures.
trapnote: One-tenth of total membership, counted with the presiding officer.

q: Consider the process for a Constitution Amendment Bill: 1-It may be introduced in either House. 2-A joint sitting may be summoned to resolve a deadlock. 3-The President must give assent to it. Which is/are correct?
expl: There is no joint sitting for an Amendment Bill; assent became mandatory in 1971.
why: The absence of a joint sitting means an Amendment Bill must pass each House separately by the required majority.
trapnote: No joint sitting for a Money Bill or an Amendment Bill. Each must clear each House on its own.

q: Which statement about the Public Accounts Committee is correct?
options: It examines the estimates of expenditure before the Budget is presented
It examines the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General
It is drawn exclusively from the lower House and has thirty members
It is chaired by the Minister of Finance by long-standing convention
expl: Its principal function is examination of the audit reports.
why: The second option describes the function of a different committee, and the fourth inverts a well-known convention.
trapnote: Audit reports go to one committee and expenditure estimates to another. Do not merge them.

q: Consider the privileges of the Houses: 1-They have been codified by a law of Parliament. 2-They include freedom of speech in the House. 3-They include immunity for publication under the authority of a House. Which is/are correct?
expl: Privileges have never been codified; the other two are accurate.
why: The Constitution contemplates codification but it has not occurred, so the privileges remain those obtaining earlier.
trapnote: Privileges remain uncodified. The Constitution contemplates a law that has never been made.

q: On the Speaker's certificate that a Bill is a Money Bill, which statement is correct?
options: It is declared final and the question has never been examined judicially
It is open to review as a matter of course in every case
It is declared final, though the correctness of that approach has been referred to a larger bench
It requires the concurrence of the Chairman of the upper House
expl: Finality is declared, but the scope of that finality is under reference.
why: The second option overstates the settledness of the position; the third overstates its reviewability.
trapnote: The text declares finality. The extent of that finality is a live question before a larger bench.

q: Consider the following on legislative procedure: 1-A Financial Bill is the same as a Money Bill. 2-A Money Bill requires the President's recommendation for introduction. 3-Only the lower House may originate a Money Bill. Which is/are correct?
expl: A Financial Bill contains other matters too and follows the ordinary procedure.
why: The distinction between the two categories of Bill is the point, and it turns on whether the Bill contains anything beyond the listed matters.
trapnote: A Money Bill contains only the listed matters. Anything more makes it a Financial Bill.

q: A member is arrested in a criminal case while the House is in session. Which statement is correct?
options: The arrest is unlawful, the member being immune while the House sits
The arrest is lawful, and the presiding officer must be informed of it
The arrest is lawful only with the prior permission of the presiding officer
The arrest is unlawful during the session and for forty days on either side
expl: Criminal arrest is lawful; the immunity is confined to civil process.
why: The fourth option applies the forty-day rule, which attaches to the civil immunity alone.
trapnote: The forty-day window belongs to the civil immunity. It has no application to criminal arrest.
